conditions.label: Traumatic epidural hemorrhage with loss of consciousness of unspecified duration, initial encounter

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily for 7 days total (last dose 3/12)
Take 2 tablets by mouth every 8 hours as needed for pain

reports.text:
Indication: motorcycle crash, unhelmeted, loss of consciousness at scene, severe headache.
Technique: axial noncontrast CT of the head with coronal and sagittal reformats.
Findings: Hyperdense biconvex extra-axial collection over the right temporal convexity that does not cross suture lines, maximal thickness 16 mm, estimated volume 34 mL. Local mass effect with 3 mm leftward midline shift. Basal cisterns patent. No subdural, subarachnoid or intraparenchymal hemorrhage. No fracture identified. Ventricles normal in size. Gray-white differentiation preserved. Paranasal sinuses and mastoid air cells clear.
reports.conclusion: Acute right temporal epidural hematoma, 16 mm maximal thickness, approximately 34 mL, with 3 mm midline shift. No other intracranial hemorrhage. No fracture identified. Neurosurgery notified at 15:31.

reports.text:
Comparison: 03/06/2026.
Findings: Interval right temporal craniotomy with evacuation of the epidural hematoma. Expected postoperative pneumocephalus and soft tissue swelling at the operative site. No residual or recurrent epidural collection. No new intracranial hemorrhage. Midline shift resolved. Basal cisterns patent.
reports.conclusion: Satisfactory evacuation of right temporal epidural hematoma. No residual or new hemorrhage.

procedures.procedure: Craniotomy for evacuation of epidural hematoma, supratentorial
Hospital discharge day management, 30 minutes or less

documents.title: Neurosurgery Admission History and Physical
documents.author: neurosurgery
documents.body:
NEUROSURGERY ADMISSION H&P
Date of service: 03/06/2026, 15:40

CC: severe headache after motorcycle crash

HPI: 23 y/o man with obstructive HCM and a history of syncope, brought in by EMS after a motorcycle crash. He was not wearing a helmet. Found unresponsive at the scene by bystanders and EMS; he woke up shortly after arrival in our ED and now complains of a severe headache. No other complaints.

PMH: obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy; syncope (2024).
PSH: none.
Meds: metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily, last dose this morning.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: father sudden cardiac death at 41; paternal uncle with HCM.
SH: university student. Never smoker. Occasional alcohol.

Exam: BP 140/90, HR 100, RR 18, T 37.0 C (98.6 F), SpO2 98% RA.
Alert and oriented to person, place and time but restless on the stretcher. Pupils equal and reactive. Extraocular movements full. Face symmetric. Full strength throughout, sensation intact, no drift. No focal neurologic deficit. Cervical collar in place, cleared after CT. Primary and secondary trauma survey otherwise negative per ED.

Imaging: CT head, acute right temporal epidural hematoma, biconvex, not crossing sutures, 16 mm thick, about 34 mL, 3 mm midline shift. CT C-spine negative.
Labs: CBC, BMP, PT/INR normal.

Assessment: Traumatic epidural hematoma, right temporal, volume over 30 mL with mass effect, after loss of consciousness at the scene.

Plan: Emergent right temporal craniotomy for evacuation. Consent obtained from the patient, mother present and informed. Anesthesia aware of obstructive HCM: maintain preload, avoid tachycardia and vasodilation. Continue metoprolol. Levetiracetam for seizure prophylaxis. Neuro ICU postoperatively.

Neurosurgery attending

documents.title: Operative Report
documents.author: neurosurgery
documents.body:
OPERATIVE REPORT
Date of surgery: 03/06/2026
Preoperative diagnosis: right temporal epidural hematoma
Postoperative diagnosis: same
Procedure: right temporal craniotomy for evacuation of epidural hematoma
Anesthesia: general endotracheal
EBL: minimal
Specimens: none
Complications: none

Indications: 23 y/o man after an unhelmeted motorcycle crash with an acute right temporal epidural hematoma of about 34 mL with midline shift.

Description: Supine, head turned left on a horseshoe rest. Right temporal question-mark incision after prep and drape. Scalp flap reflected, bone flap turned with the craniotome. Acute epidural clot encountered and evacuated with suction and irrigation. Bleeding points coagulated. Dura intact, tacked up circumferentially. Hemostasis confirmed. Bone flap replaced with plates. Subgaleal drain placed. Galea closed with interrupted sutures, skin with staples. Sterile dressing.

The patient tolerated the procedure well, extubated in the OR, moving all extremities, to the neuro ICU in stable condition. Anesthesia reported stable hemodynamics on preload support; metoprolol continued.

Neurosurgery attending

documents.title: Discharge Summary
documents.author: neurosurgery
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted: 03/06/2026  Discharged: 03/10/2026
Service: Neurosurgery

Principal diagnosis: traumatic right temporal epidural hematoma
Other: obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy; history of syncope
Procedure: right temporal craniotomy with evacuation of epidural hematoma, 03/06/2026

Course: Arrived after an unhelmeted motorcycle crash with loss of consciousness at the scene, regaining consciousness in the ED, with severe headache and a 34 mL right temporal epidural hematoma on CT. Taken emergently to the OR the same afternoon for craniotomy and evacuation, uncomplicated. Postoperative day 1 CT showed satisfactory evacuation without residual or new hemorrhage. Two nights in the neuro ICU, then the neurosurgery floor. Drain removed POD 1. Neurologically intact throughout. Headache settled to mild by POD 2 on acetaminophen alone. Levetiracetam for 7 days of seizure prophylaxis. Metoprolol continued at home dose with stable heart rate and blood pressure. Ambulating independently, tolerating diet. CT cervical spine negative; no other injuries identified.

Condition at discharge: good. Alert, oriented, no focal deficit. Incision clean, staples in place.

Allergies: NKDA

Discharge medications:
- Metoprolol succinate ER 50 mg daily (unchanged)
- Levetiracetam 500 mg twice daily, last dose 03/12/2026
- Acetaminophen 1000 mg every 8 hours as needed for pain

Instructions: no heavy lifting or contact activity until neurosurgery follow-up. Keep the incision dry for 48 hours, then gentle washing. Staple removal in 7 to 10 days, at the PCP office is fine. Wear a helmet when riding. Return for worsening headache, vomiting, confusion, weakness or seizure.

Follow-up: neurosurgery clinic in about 4 weeks with CT head. PCP within one week.

Neurosurgery

documents.title: Transitional care call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: TCM call, discharged yesterday after craniotomy for epidural hematoma. Spoke with pt, mother on speaker. Home, resting. Headache mild, acetaminophen twice yesterday. No vomiting, no confusion, no weakness, no seizure. Taking levetiracetam twice a day through tomorrow and his metoprolol. Incision dry, staples in. Discharge papers reviewed with them; med list reconciled, matches. PCP visit booked Fri 3/13 2:00, staple removal can be done then or the following week. Return precautions reviewed.

documents.title: Post-hospital visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Post-discharge. Admitted 3/6 to 3/10 at an outside hospital, neurosurgery service: unhelmeted motorcycle crash, LOC at the scene, right temporal epidural hematoma about 34 mL with 3 mm shift, emergent right temporal craniotomy and evacuation same day. POD1 CT clean. Discharge summary, op note and H&P reviewed.

Today: here with his mother. Headache gone the last day or so, took acetaminophen once yesterday. No nausea, vomiting, confusion, weakness, numbness or vision change. Sleeping fine. Finished levetiracetam last night. Still on metoprolol succinate 50 daily. No syncope.

Meds: metoprolol succinate ER 50 mg daily; acetaminophen 1000 mg q8h prn. NKDA.

Exam: vitals as charted. Alert, oriented, conversational, appropriate. Right temporal curvilinear incision with staples, clean, dry, no erythema or drainage, no fluid collection. Pupils equal and reactive, EOM full, face symmetric, strength and sensation normal, gait steady. Heart regular, systolic murmur LLSB as before. Lungs clear.

A/P
1. Traumatic epidural hematoma s/p craniotomy 3/6, recovering well, intact. Staples out Tuesday 3/17 with nursing. Neurosurgery f/u with CT in April, scheduled. Activity per neurosurgery: no lifting or contact. Helmet, every time, if he rides again; we talked about it plainly.
2. Obstructive HCM: stable through the admission. Cardiology annual had been booked for March; he'll reschedule after neurosurgery clears him.
3. Med rec done.

documents.title: Staple removal
documents.author: RN
documents.body: 11 days post right temporal craniotomy. Staples removed without difficulty. Incision well approximated and healed along its length, no erythema, drainage or gaps. Steri-strips not needed. Pt feels well, no headache. Told him he can wash his hair normally now. Reminded about neurosurgery visit in April.

documents.title: letter for school
documents.author: patient
documents.body: The dean of students office wants a letter saying I was in the hospital and when I can come back to class. Can you write one? I feel ready

documents.title: Medical letter for university
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
To the Dean of Students:

Rowan Doherty is a patient of this practice. He was hospitalized from March 6 through March 10, 2026, and has been recovering at home since. He is medically able to return to classes and coursework now. He should not take part in contact sports or heavy physical activity until cleared by his surgical team. Please extend reasonable accommodations for the work missed during this period.

Primary care physician

documents.title: RE: letter for school
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Letter is attached, you can forward it to the dean's office. Glad you're feeling ready.

Comparison: 03/07/2026.
Findings: Postoperative changes of right temporal craniotomy with bone flap in place. Resolution of the previously evacuated epidural collection; no residual extra-axial fluid. Postoperative pneumocephalus resolved. No intracranial hemorrhage. No mass effect. Ventricles and sulci normal.
reports.conclusion: Resolved right temporal epidural hematoma. Expected postoperative changes only.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Neurosurgery Clinic Follow-up
documents.author: neurosurgery
documents.body:
Neurosurgery clinic
Date of visit: 04/13/2026

Dear colleague,

Rowan is five weeks out from right temporal craniotomy for evacuation of a traumatic epidural hematoma. He feels back to normal. No headaches, no seizures, no new neurological symptoms. He is attending classes. Medications: metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily. Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: incision fully healed, flap contour good. Alert and oriented, speech fluent, cranial nerves intact, strength and sensation normal, gait normal.

CT head today: resolution of the epidural hematoma; postoperative changes only.

Impression: traumatic epidural hematoma, resolved after evacuation. Excellent recovery.

Plan: cleared for normal activity, including classes and exercise within his cardiology limits. We discussed helmet use at length. No routine neurosurgical follow-up needed; we are happy to see him again for any concerns.

Sincerely,
Neurosurgery

documents.title: Neurosurgery visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Read the neurosurgery note: CT shows the bleed is completely gone and they've cleared you for everything. Really good news. Next step is getting the cardiology visit rebooked.

reports.text: Complete 2D, color and spectral Doppler study, compared with 03/18/2024. Normal LV cavity size. Asymmetric septal hypertrophy, maximal septal thickness 21 mm. LVEF 70%. Systolic anterior motion of the anterior mitral leaflet. Resting LVOT peak gradient 35 mmHg, 62 mmHg with Valsalva. Mitral and aortic valves structurally normal. Right ventricle normal in size and function. Atria normal in size. No pericardial effusion.
reports.conclusion: Obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, unchanged: septum 21 mm, LVEF 70%, LVOT gradient 35 mmHg at rest and 62 mmHg with Valsalva.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Cardiology Annual Follow-up
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Cardiology clinic
Date of visit: 06/08/2026

Dear colleague,

Rowan's annual visit was moved from March because of his admission for a traumatic epidural hematoma, treated with craniotomy on 3/6/2026; he has recovered fully and neurosurgery has discharged him. From a cardiac standpoint he has had no syncope since March 2024 and no exertional chest pain, dyspnea or palpitations. Medications: metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily. Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: vital signs as recorded. Healed right temporal scar. Systolic murmur at the left lower sternal border, unchanged. Lungs clear. No edema.

Echo today: septum 21 mm, EF 70%, outflow gradient 35 mmHg at rest and 62 mmHg with Valsalva, unchanged.

Impression: obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, stable. Syncope, no recurrence.

Plan: continue metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily. Activity guidance unchanged. Return in one year.

Sincerely,
Outpatient cardiology
